sentences.text: THIS MFA FILED U/S. 173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING ALLOW THIS APPEAL AND MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 04.01.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO.267/2015 BY THE ADDL.DIST.
AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND ADDL.MACT AT BIDAR (SITTING AT BHALKI) AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION FROM RS.70,000/- WITH 6 INTEREST TO RS.14,99,000/- WITH 12 INTEREST.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimants challenging the correctness of the judgment and award dated 04.01.2019 passed by the Addl. District Judge and Addl. MACT, Bidar (Sitting at Bhalki) in MVC No.267/2015.
2.
The claimants are the legal representatives of deceased Ramchander Rao.
They claimed that on 03.03.2015, the deceased and claimant No.1 were waiting for a bus to reach Bhalki to attend to their personal work.
At about, 12.15 p.m., a lorry bearing registration No.AP- 25/W-9417 driven in a rash and negligent manner from Bhalki side dashed against the deceased Ramchander Rao.

As a result,
he suffered injuries and was declared brought dead at Government Hospital, Bidar.
The jurisdictional police registered a case in crime No.41/2015 for the offence punishable under Sections 279, 304-A of IPC r/w Section 187 of IMV Act.
The claimants alleged that the deceased Ramchander Rao was running a grocery shop and was earning a sum of Rs.12,000/- per month.
They claimed that the deceased was 65 years and was contributing his entire income towards maintenance of the claimants and their families.

They alleged that due to sudden death of Ramchander Rao, they suffered mental and financial distress and therefore filed a claim petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The claim was resisted by the insurer who denied the accident as well as the entitlement of the claimants to claim the compensation, as they were not the dependants of the deceased.
3. The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P8.

The insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 who marked Exs.R1 and R2.
4.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the tribunal held that the claimants were not dependant on the deceased as they are all majors by age and work independent.

The tribunal therefore refused to grant any compensation to the claimants towards loss of dependency but awarded the following compensation; Sl.No. Heads of Compensation Amount in Rs. 1 Loss of estate 15,000/-
2. Funeral expenses 15,000/-

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is filed.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submitted that the claimants were dependent sons as the deceased was running a grocery store and was contributing all his income towards the maintenance of the family of the claimants.

He submits that the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Birendar and Others reported in 2020 Kant MAC 225 (SC), considered the very same question and held so long as the claimants are the legal representatives of the deceased, they are entitled to claim compensation on account of the death of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Birendar and Others reported in 2020 Kant MAC 225 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He, therefore submits that the judgment and award passed by the tribunal warrants interference and the compensation towards loss of dependency deserves to be granted to the claimants by treating the notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- as per the chart prescribed for settlement of cases before the Lok Adalath.
7.

Learned counsel for the respondent-insurer on the other hand contended that the dependency of the claimants is an essential fact that has to be proved to claim compensation for loss of dependency and since the claimants were all majors by age and earning, they were not dependant on the income of the deceased and thus the tribunal was justified in not awarding compensation towards loss of dependency.
8. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.
9. The relationship of the claimants with the deceased is not in dispute.
The claimants have claimed that the deceased was running grocery store from which he was earning Rs.12,000/- to Rs.15,000/-.
It is quite natural that when the deceased and the claimants were residing under the same roof, it is possible that the deceased could have contributed to the maintenance of the family.

Even otherwise,
the Apex Court in the aforesaid case has considered the said question and has held that once the relationship of the claimants with the deceased is proved, the claimants would be naturally dependent on the deceased and therefore the tribunal was not justified in not awarding compensation towards loss of dependency.
10. In view of the above, the compensation towards loss of dependency deserves to be awarded by treating the notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month.
The deceased had left behind the claimants as his dependants and therefore 1/3rd of his income is liable to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
The deceased was 65 years and the applicable multiplier is 5.

sentences.text: Sl. No.

Heads of Compensation Amount in Rs. 1 Loss of dependency: 3,20,000/-
(Rs.8,000/- x 12 x 5 x 2/3)
2. Loss of estate 15,000/-
3. Funeral expenses 15,000/-
4. Loss of Parental consortium Rs.40,000/-
Total 3,90,000/-
11.
In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.70,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.3,90,000/-.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.3,20,000/- is payable by respondent No.2 - Insurance Company along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The insurer-respondent No.2 shall deposit the enhanced compensation with interest before the Tribunal within one month from the date of receipt of this judgment.
12. Out of the enhanced compensation, 50% of the same shall be deposited in the name of the appellants/claimants in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 is permitted to file his memo of appearance/vakalath within a period two weeks.
